title: Inverse image equals tensor pullback to the inverse-image ring
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map of topological spaces, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $Y$, and $K^\bullet$ a cochain complex of $R$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Use the canonical inverse-image modules [def-pc-topological-inverse-image-module] and their functor $I_f$ [lem-pc-inverse-image-module-functor-exact]. Equip $(X,f^{-1}R)\to(Y,R)$ with structure map $R\to f_*f^{-1}R$ equal to the inverse-image adjunction unit. The termwise tensor pullback, defined using sheaf change of rings [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], is isomorphic as a complex of $f^{-1}R$-modules to $I_f(K^\bullet)$. This assertion assumes neither K-flatness nor exactness of $K^\bullet$.

source.place: Tag 008A (lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict), Section 0094 (section-ringed-spaces-functoriality-modules); the identity adjoint ring map case used in Cohomology Tag 06YC

proof.text: The adjoint ring map of the inverse-image unit is the identity on the inverse-image ring, by Adjunction.homEquiv_symm_unit.

In each section ring A, ModuleCat.extendScalarsId identifies extension along the identity with the original module, with inverse m mapped to 1 tensor m. The characterized changeOfRingsMap sends that tensor to 1 tensor the restricted m, because ring restrictions preserve 1. PresheafOfModules.isoMk assembles the resulting presheaf-module isomorphisms.
Sheafify this isomorphism and compose with the module-sheafification counit isomorphism on the original sheaf. This identifies changeOfRings along the identity with the original module.

ModuleCat.extendScalarsId.inv.naturality proves compatibility with module morphisms before sheafification. Cancel the invertible presheaf-module components, apply functoriality of module sheafification, and then apply naturality of the sheafification counit. This gives naturality of the sheaf-level isomorphism for changeOfRingsHom.

Transport the identity-ring isomorphism along the adjoint-ring-map equality. Apply the naturality just proved to every differential in the canonical inverse-image complex. HomologicalComplex.Hom.isoOfComponents yields the required isomorphism of complexes.
